query_database.py:186-203. users is incremented synchronously with entry creation (no await between), so no cancellation can land between creation and the try. Cancellation or error in acquire hits the except BaseException branch (194-197), which calls _release_queue_entry. After acquire returns there is no await before the try/finally (199-203), so a cancellation cannot be delivered in that gap. Any body exit, including raise or cancel, runs the finally, which releases the lock and then calls _release_queue_entry. asyncio.Lock.release raises only RuntimeError when the lock is unlocked. That cannot happen here because this call holds the lock. _release_queue_entry (152-162) deletes the entry when users <= 0, and the identity check protects successor entries. The conversation_id None path creates no entry. Hostile input traced: a waiter cancelled in acquire, with the holder finishing concurrently. Both paths decrement users, and the last one deletes the entry.

Skipped rollbacks in query_database._rollback_conversation (no seam or store raises) leave the messages present, so updated_at doesn't reflect absent messages there either. Whole-conversation eviction (_remember) removes the conversation itself. No other method deletes individual messages. The ValueError on length<0 happens before any mutation.

query_database.py:152-203. _conversation_turn increments entry.users before acquire (190) and every exit path decrements exactly once: BaseException during acquire (194-197, covers cancelled waiter) or the finally after yield (201-203). _release_queue_entry (160-162) deletes only if users<=0 and the registry still maps the id to that same entry, so a superseded entry is left alone and a late release cannot delete a successor. Because users counts waiters, an entry is never deleted while a waiter is parked, so a second lock is never minted. Hostile input traced: cancel a queued waiter. Its increment is undone, and the entry is deleted if it was the last user. Increments and decrements are paired and there is no await between the read-modify-write steps, so the count cannot go negative.

criteria.json is a valid list with criterion 4 matching this item, so it counts. (b) The except-BaseException arm -> releases the claim, so the criterion's outcome holds. (c) The finally arm -> releases, so the outcome holds.
